facts.text: The silver gull is the most common gull in Australia, found throughout the continent, especially near the coast.
facts.quote: It is the most common gull of Australia. It has been found throughout the continent, but particularly at or near coastal areas.

facts.text: An adult silver gull has a white head, body and tail, with light grey wings tipped in black with white spots.
facts.quote: The head, body, and tail of an adult silver gull are white, and the wings are light grey with white-spotted, black tips.

facts.text: Adults have bright red beaks that become even brighter during breeding or as the bird ages.
facts.quote: Adults have bright red beaks which gets brighter during breeding or when they get older.

facts.text: The silver gull's most common call is a harsh, high pitched 'kwarwh', part of a varied repertoire.
facts.quote: The silver gull has a sharp voice consisting of a variety of calls. The most common call is a harsh, high pitched 'kwarwh'.

facts.text: It naturally eats worms, fish, insects and crustaceans, but is also a successful scavenger around people.
facts.quote: The silver gull naturally feeds on worms, fish, insects and crustaceans. It is a successful scavenger, allowing increased numbers near human settlements.

facts.text: Silver gulls are known to pester humans for chips and steal unattended food.
facts.quote: It is known to pester humans for chips and steal unattended food.

facts.text: Breeding from August to December, they nest in large colonies on offshore islands, with both parents sharing all duties.
facts.quote: Breeding occurs from August to December, typically in large colonies on offshore islands.

facts.text: A typical clutch holds one to three eggs, and a pair often raises two broods in a year.
facts.quote: Typical clutch size is one to three eggs. Often two broods are raised in a year, and both adults share nest-building, incubation and feeding.

facts.text: Silver gulls thrive in urban environments, doing so well that nesting grounds are the only limit on their population growth.
facts.quote: Their successful adaption to urban habitats have seen their population increase in areas of human activity, with the availability of nesting grounds the only limiting factor on population growth.

facts.text: The nest sits on the ground and is built from seaweed, roots and plant stems, sometimes placed in shrubs, rocks or jetties.
facts.quote: The nest is located on the ground and consists of seaweed, roots, and plant stems. The nests may be found in low shrubs, rocks and jetties.
